The bug causing `org.apache.commons.lang.time.DateUtilsTest::testTruncateLang59` to fail has been diagnosed and resolved.

### Root Cause
In [`DateUtils.modify(Calendar, int, boolean)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_a_blind/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L619-L740):
1. During Daylight Saving Time (DST) transition periods (such as the repeated fall-back hour), invoking `Calendar.set(field, ...)` causes `Calendar` to recalculate its internal millisecond offset and default to standard time instead of preserving daylight saving time, shifting the time by an hour.
2. Truncating milliseconds, seconds, and minutes using `Calendar` field setting directly triggered this recalculation. Truncating these sub-hour fields should be done directly on the epoch milliseconds (`val.getTime()`).
3. Calling `val.set(fields[i][0], val.get(fields[i][0]) - offset)` even when `offset == 0` marked fields as modified in the `Calendar` instance, triggering unnecessary recalculations during DST overlap hours.

### Fix
1. Early return if `field == Calendar.MILLISECOND`.
2. Implement manual millisecond/second/minute truncation directly via epoch time calculations on `Date.getTime()`.
3. Guard the field update `val.set(...)` with `if (offset != 0)` to prevent resetting unmodified fields.

The focused patch has been generated and saved to `blind_fix.patch`. All tests pass cleanly.
